# Part I: R Foundations {.unnumbered}

This part teaches the R language itself. It assumes no knowledge of programming. We start with R as a calculator, and move step by step to objects, subsetting, functions, pipes, conditions and loops, and functional programming.

The examples are small, but they are chosen with audit in mind. Along the way you will meet the traps behind most errors in audit analysis. An amount is read as text. An account number loses its leading zero. A total silently becomes `NA`. Two decimals do not compare as equal.

These chapters build on one another, so read them in order.

:::: {.chapter-cards}
